description: We are a multidisciplinary team focused on solving complex problems through software development, engineering, and geospatial data analysis. Driven by technical curiosity, persistent effort, and continuous learning, we transform satellite data into high-impact strategic decisions.
summary:
TerraTerm turns NASA’s flood of Earth data into clear answers: what is changing, where, by how much, and whether the change is statistically significant.
A single climate driver like El Niño can flood one region while drying another at the same time. In Peru, our pilot case, the northern coast suffers extreme rain and disease outbreaks while the southern highlands face severe drought. Current tools don’t detect these opposite trends automatically, regionally and with statistical rigor.
TerraTerm is a web platform with an interactive 3D globe and a 2D country map:
Data: it queries NASA POWER variables (MERRA-2 surface temperature and precipitation) and cross-checks them with GPM IMERG.
Computation: it computes every region’s and ocean cell’s trend using Sen’s slope and the Mann-Kendall test.
Visualization: it paints a real thermal-trend map, provides an interactive ranking and automatically detects dipoles between regions.
Context: it analyzes ocean–land correlation.
Assistant: a bilingual AI explains the results with their sources.
details:
Functionality: Ranging from a 3D globe to localized analysis, TerraTerm queries temperature data from NASA POWER and calculates statistical trends (Sen’s slope and Mann-Kendall test) by region and ocean. It visualizes significant warming or cooling on a 2D map, detects thermal dipoles by comparing two zones, and interprets the data via a bilingual AI assistant.

Benefits and Impact: It democratizes complex climate data in seconds, ensuring source transparency and offering mobile access without the need for registration. It assists farmers, fishers, and local authorities—starting in Peru with global scalability—in anticipating extreme weather events and marine warming.

Tech Stack: Frontend: React 19, Vite, Tailwind CSS 4, Three.js (R3F), d3-geo, TopoJSON, Recharts, Zustand, and Framer Motion. Backend: Vercel Serverless and Vercel AI SDK (Gemini/OpenAI). It utilizes data from NASA (POWER, GPM IMERG, Blue Marble) and geoBoundaries.

Innovation and Quality: The platform stands out for its ability to automatically detect thermal dipoles, filter maps based on statistical significance, and enable zone comparisons in just two taps via a contextual AI assistant. It adheres to WMO statistical standards, secures API keys on the server side, optimizes performance by reducing ~250 individual queries to 6 regional requests through caching, includes an offline mode, ensures accessibility (ARIA compliance), and is fully bilingual.
